summary.text: Sam Montaño is a Democratic state representative from the 15th Suffolk District who has served in the Massachusetts House of Representatives since January 2023 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A community organizer before taking office, Montaño worked on affordable housing and environmental justice in Jamaica Plain, Mission Hill, Chelsea and Roxbury.

paragraphs.text: Sam Montaño earned a bachelor's degree from the University of California, Los Angeles, in 2013.

According to the Legislature's biography, Montaño worked at a women's shelter before moving into community organizing at the Jamaica Plain Neighborhood Development Corporation and later became Director of Organizing for GreenRoots, a nonprofit focused on environmental justice.
Montaño took office on January 4, 2023, succeeding Nika Elugardo.

Montaño is vice chair of the Joint Committee on Aging and Independence and also serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means and the Joint Committees on Municipalities and Regional Government, Public Health, and Ways and Means.
